title: Decoded Audiotec Fischer .pct6 tune
description: Structure produced by pct6_extract.py when it decodes an Audiotec Fischer DSP PC-Tool 6 (.pct6) setup file. See FINDINGS.md in this repository for the container format and what each field means. v1 is additive-only: existing fields keep their meaning forever; a breaking change gets a v2 schema alongside this one, never an edit in place - so pinning to this URL is safe long-term.

$schema.description: Always this schema's own $id - lets any validator resolve the right version without being told which one to use.

source_file.description: Original .pct6 filename this data was decoded from.

decoder.description: Tool and version that produced this file, e.g. "pct6_extract.py v1.0.0".

container_mode.description: Which of PC-Tool's five container variants matched, per the FINDINGS.md table (plain XML, plain qCompress, or qCompress XORed with the ATFV6 / ATFV6P / ATF key).

xml_bytes.description: Size in bytes of the decompressed XML payload.

meta.description: Verbatim attributes of the XML root <ATF> element. All values are strings, as stored in the XML - convert numeric-looking ones yourself. Known keys documented here; additional keys appear on other PC-Tool versions/devices and should be kept, not dropped.

V.description: PC-Tool version that saved the file, e.g. "6.03.04".

FN.description: Original full path of the file on the machine that saved it.

outputs.description: One entry per <OC> element - every physical output the device exposes, whether or not it carries non-default settings. Filter on eq_band_count/highpass/lowpass/delay_raw/gain_db to find the ones actually in use.

inputs.description: One entry per <IC> element - every physical input.

labels.description: Optional, hand-maintained annotation layer. Nothing under here is decoded from the .pct6 file - it is inferred (from crossover ranges, delay symmetry, etc.) or supplied by whoever is editing this data file. Safe to extend, safe to omit. For the channel naming the file does carry - the Digital Routing speaker assignment, e.g. "Front L High" - use channel_name instead; this layer is for annotation that goes beyond it, such as the actual driver type fitted.

by_output_index.description: Keyed by the output's "index" field (as a string) from the outputs array.

side.description: e.g. L, R, or a named zone.

role.description: Which XML element this came from: <OC> (output) or <IC> (input). The two share this shape but differ in which attributes are meaningful - see enabled/delay_group/link_group below.

index.description: Output number (ON attribute) for role=output, or input number (IN attribute) for role=input. -1 if the attribute was missing.

channel_id.description: Internal channel id (CN attribute). Stable identifier distinct from index; resolve it to a name via channel_name.

channel_name.description: Name assigned to this channel, resolved from channel_id (CN) against PC-Tool's channel-name tables (documented in FINDINGS.md). Outputs and inputs use separate id spaces, so the same channel_id resolves differently depending on role. For an output this is the speaker type selected on the Digital Routing page - e.g. "Front L High", "Front R Mid", "Subwoofer 1", or "Not assigned". Read out of the file, not inferred (contrast the labels object). null if channel_id is outside the known list, e.g. on a newer PC-Tool build that defines more entries.

enabled.description: Channel-enable flag (CE attribute). Only meaningful for role=output - <IC> elements carry no such flag, so this is null for inputs.

delay_group.description: DG attribute. Output-only; null for inputs.

link_group.description: LG attribute. Output-only; null for inputs.

gain_db.description: Channel gain in dB, derived as 20*log10(gain_linear). -Infinity if gain_linear is 0.

gain_linear.description: Channel gain exactly as stored (the <Vol L="..."> attribute) - a linear amplitude multiplier, 1.0 = 0 dB.

delay_raw.description: Raw stored delay value (the <T ... T="..."> attribute), unit unconfirmed - see delay_ms/delay_cm.

delay_ms.description: delay_raw interpreted as samples at 96 kHz (ACO DSPs' native rate) and converted to milliseconds. UNCONFIRMED - see FINDINGS.md 'Open questions'. If the true unit differs, this scales linearly with delay_raw so relative comparisons between channels stay valid even if the absolute unit is off.

delay_cm.description: Same delay_raw conversion, expressed as an equivalent path-length difference at 343 m/s. Same caveat as delay_ms.

highpass.description: The channel's highpass crossover slot, or null if none is active (bypassed or 0 dB/oct).

lowpass.description: The channel's lowpass crossover slot, or null if none is active.

eq_bands.description: Active parametric peaking bands only - default/untouched slots (gain 0 dB, Q 4.3) are filtered out.

eq_band_count.description: Length of eq_bands, provided for convenience.

raw_attrib.description: Every attribute of the source <OC>/<IC> element, verbatim and unconverted, so fields this schema doesn't yet model (e.g. Finit, MT, GD, HPi, LPi - default-filter and mode indices that don't bear on EQ/crossover/delay/gain) are preserved rather than silently dropped.

filter.description: One <Fil> slot. A channel has up to 30: a fixed highpass+lowpass crossover pair plus up to 28 parametric peaking bands.

type_id.description: Raw T attribute. 1=unused, 9/10=Butterworth LP/HP, 11/12=Bessel LP/HP, 13/14=Tschebyscheff LP/HP, 15/16=Linkwitz-Riley LP/HP, 17=parametric peak. See FINDINGS.md.

label.description: Human-readable name for type_id, e.g. "Lowpass Linkwitz".

gain_db.description: For kind=peak: band gain in dB. For kind=lowpass/highpass: crossover slope in dB/octave (e.g. -24 = 4th-order/24 dB per octave), not a level.

q.description: Q factor. Crossover slots typically read 0.7 (Butterworth-derived); peaking bands vary.

bypassed.description: Per-slot bypass (FilBy attribute) - independent of the channel-wide eq_bypassed flag.
